Celebratory Rice

Served at: Nowruz

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 45 min

Celebratory Rice, known as 'Polo' in Persian cuisine, is a fragrant and colorful rice dish traditionally served during Nowruz, the Persian New Year. It symbolizes renewal and prosperity, featuring a blend of aromatic spices, nuts, and dried fruits to welcome the new year with abundance and joy.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups basmati rice (uncooked)
  • 4 cups water
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, crushed and soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
  • 1/4 cup vegetable oil or butter
  • 1/2 cup slivered almonds
  • 1/2 cup pistachios, chopped
  • 1/2 cup dried barberries or dried cranberries
  • 1/4 cup sugar
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom

Method

  1. Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch.
  2. In a large pot, bring 4 cups of water to a boil and add 1/2 teaspoon salt.
  3. Add the rinsed rice to the boiling water and cook for 6-8 minutes until the rice is partially cooked but still firm (al dente).
  4. Drain the rice in a colander and rinse briefly with warm water to stop the cooking process.
  5. In the same pot, heat the vegetable oil or butter over medium heat.
  6. Add half of the partially cooked rice to the pot, then sprinkle half of the saffron water evenly over the rice.
  7. Layer the remaining rice on top and pour the rest of the saffron water over it.
  8. Cover the pot with a clean kitchen towel and place the lid tightly on top to trap steam.
  9. Cook the rice on low heat for 30-35 minutes to allow it to steam and develop a crispy golden crust (tahdig) at the bottom.
  10. While the rice cooks, toast the slivered almonds and pistachios in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant and lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes.
  11. In a small pan, combine dried barberries, sugar, cinnamon, and cardamom with 2 tablespoons of water and cook over low heat for 3-4 minutes until the barberries soften and the sugar dissolves.
  12. Once the rice is done, gently fluff it with a fork and transfer to a serving platter.
  13. Top the rice with the toasted nuts and the sweetened barberries mixture before serving.

Tips

  • For a traditional crispy tahdig, use thinly sliced potatoes or flatbread at the bottom of the pot before adding rice.
  • If barberries are unavailable, dried cranberries or currants make a good substitute.
  • Soaking the rice for 30 minutes before cooking can help achieve a fluffier texture.
